verdict: Only if you can run a tight kitchen and build repeat customers outside the apps. Cloud kitchens have low entry costs, which is why so many open and close within two years. After aggregator commissions, discounts and food costs, a well-run kitchen keeps ₹10–40 on a ₹300 order, so success depends on repeat orders and direct ordering.
angle: Multi-brand cloud kitchens, which run several menus from one kitchen, were the big trend a few years ago. Many of those operators have since cut back to one or two strong brands. The kitchens doing well in 2026 pick one cuisine they can own in a small delivery radius, keep the menu short, and use WhatsApp, ONDC apps or office lunch plans to cut their dependence on aggregators.

faq.q: How much does it cost to start a cloud kitchen in India?
faq.a: A single-brand cloud kitchen in a small rented space costs ₹3–8 lakh, including equipment, licences, packaging and launch discounts. Rent is the biggest variable.

faq.q: How much commission do Swiggy and Zomato charge?
faq.a: Commission plus fees commonly adds up to 25–30% of the order value, and paid visibility and discounts come on top. Check the current terms with each platform before you set menu prices.

faq.q: What licences does a cloud kitchen need?
faq.a: FSSAI registration or licence, a trade licence, fire NOC, Shops and Establishments registration and GST. Aggregators ask for these during onboarding.

faq.q: Why do most cloud kitchens fail?
faq.a: The most common reasons are launching too many brands too early, relying on discounts for orders, and food costs creeping above 35% of menu prices.
